references.text: Jesus says the same words to the sinful woman: 'Your faith has saved you. Go in peace!' ([ref:Luk 7:50|Luke 7:50]). The expression "ἡ πίστις σου σέσωκέν σε" recurs as a fixed formula when Jesus confirms that faith is decisive for salvation and healing.
Jesus also says to the woman with the issue of blood: 'Your faith has saved you' ([ref:Luk 8:48|Luke 8:48]). The same wording is used regarding healing that comes through faith.

To the blind man at Jericho, Jesus says: 'Your faith has saved you' ([ref:Luk 18:42|Luke 18:42]). Here too, healing is directly linked to the sick person's faith, using an identical Greek formulation.

Mark's parallel account of the healing of the woman with the issue of blood: 'Your faith has saved you. Go in peace' ([ref:Mark 5:34|Mark 5:34]). The same expression "ἡ πίστις σου σέσωκέν σε" is used.
Mark's account of blind Bartimaeus: 'Your faith has saved you' ([ref:Mark 10:52|Mark 10:52]). Once again, the same formula as in Luke 17:19.

The full context of Jesus' words: The ten lepers were healed ([ref:Luk 17:11-19|Luke 17:11-19]), but only one – a Samaritan – returned to give thanks. Jesus highlights that his faith brought not only physical healing, but salvation in a deeper sense.

Naaman the Syrian was healed of leprosy when he obeyed the prophet Elisha and washed himself in the Jordan ([ref:2 Kong 5:14|2 Kings 5:14]). The similarity is striking: a foreigner healed of leprosy through obedience and faith. Jesus himself refers to Naaman in [ref:Luk 4:27|Luke 4:27].

Jesus says to the woman with the issue of blood: 'Take heart, daughter! Your faith has saved you' ([ref:Matt 9:22|Matthew 9:22]). Matthew's version of the same formula that recurs throughout the Gospels.

'The prayer of faith will save the sick, and the Lord will raise them up' ([ref:Jak 5:15|James 5:15]). Faith as a means to healing and salvation, in line with Jesus' words that 'your faith has saved you'.
'For by grace you have been saved through faith' ([ref:Ef 2:8|Ephesians 2:8]). Paul emphasizes the same principle that Jesus expresses here: salvation is linked to faith.
